Same task, five ways, measured by the RK7(8) card: two-body Kepler orbits (mu = 1, float64) from periapsis, a = 1, e uniform in [0, 0.9], random orientation; adaptive RKF7(8) (Fehlberg's tableau, a mixed absolute/relative max-norm error control and a standard step-size controller). Largest batch shown: N = 1,000,000.

| tool | lines | what it brings here |
|---|---:|---|
| hawk + eagle | 22 | the attempt is per-sample scalar code (22 lines with its launch; the kernel finishes its own samples), one kernel per attempt looped on the device: 23.5 s. |
| CuPy | 25 | array code in the NumPy style (25 lines), the control flow as masks over the batch: 182 s. |
| PyTorch | 27 | the same array formulation in PyTorch (27 lines), running where a PyTorch model already runs: 184 s. |
| JAX | 25 | writes the per-sample loop directly (25 lines) and compiles the whole batch into one executable: 40.2 s. |
| Warp | 74 | an explicit per-thread loop in a Python-embedded kernel language (74 lines, its own stages): 26.3 s. |

Full code for all five, side by side: [where RAPTOR fits](where_raptor_fits.md).
